primary_objective: Deliver the user's requested outcome at or above the required quality in the minimum practical wall-clock time.
quality_rule: Speed and utilization are means. Do not trade away required output quality merely to increase activity.

boot: Read the current durable pointer and this runtime core.
Load only the policy or evidence needed for the next concrete decision; do not restore the entire control plane by default.
Detect genuine duplicate authority or destructive overlap. Clock jitter or stale follower projections alone are not authority conflicts.
Attempt the current authority/checkpoint write when required. If it transiently fails, fence only the side effects that require authoritative commit and continue safe useful work when possible.
work: Select the highest-value safe checkpointable unit that advances the user's goal.
Prefer execution over meta-work unless meta-work removes a measured bottleneck or protects correctness.
Keep chaining useful work while the invocation remains healthy and useful authorized work exists.
Checkpoint enough to make interruption cheap; logging volume is not itself progress.
close: Stop starting large new units near the current runtime budget.
Persist the smallest sufficient resumable checkpoint.
Use the currently selected continuation adapter to secure the next wake.
Verify the adapter result when supported, then end the invocation.
recover: Limit failure impact to the failed capability or side effect.
Full BLOCKED is justified only when no safe useful work can continue, explicit user input is required, the program is terminal, or the platform prevents further execution.
Follower projections may lag and should be repaired asynchronously unless they threaten authoritative correctness.

policy_layering.adaptive_defaults: Tunable values chosen from observed runtime results.
policy_layering.adapters: Replaceable implementation mechanisms such as the wake provider.
policy_layering.ux: Plan preview, natural-language reports, onboarding, and blocker presentation; excluded from the runtime hot path unless user interaction is actually required.

incident_policy: Preserve incident lessons as regression evidence/tests where possible instead of accumulating one-off runtime prohibitions.
